## Decision record: what the converter face promises, and what its receipts look like

::: {.callout .callout-note}
**Decision.** CS-18 is a witness, not a specification: it freezes what the
exported `ms_convert()` generic and its `MsSignature` method actually
adjudicate over planted signature-and-opportunity calls, so future drift
speaks immediately. It commits only machine-stable facts: the error CLASS
always, and the message CLAUSES verbatim -- every one of them. The
converter is pure R over a bundled frequency table -- no file path beyond
the packaged extdata, no clock and no RNG touches its verdicts -- so the
ledger was DET-proved byte-stable across probe reruns. But the ACCEPTED
arms return a real float matrix: the face divides by the source
opportunities and multiplies by the target ones, so the return is a
`double` matrix whose kernel round-trip error measures ~1e-16. Under the
D11 cross-platform posture no float payload can ride a byte-committed
column, so the accepted renders commit a DISCRETE column-sum GLYPH
(`0`/`1`/`?` at a 1e-9 threshold, seven orders above the observed float
error) instead of the numbers themselves; integer, label, logical, class
and clause bytes are byte-committed, floats are censused finite/in-domain
only. The lane also refuses its own sketches: the census and ordering
claims below are read from the committed witnesses, not from the build
plan -- the runner's own degen rail caught a clause-head literal that had
been drafted one word short (see the honest section) before any witness
byte was burned.
:::

### The face

`ms_convert(signatures, from = "human-genome", to = "human-exome")` is the
exported S7 generic that re-expresses SBS96 signatures relative to a
different mutation-opportunity vector (the sigfit `convert_signatures`
semantics: divide by the source opportunities, multiply by the target
ones, re-normalize each column). It accepts a `96 x k` numeric matrix with
SBS96 registry rownames, or an `MsSignature`; the `from`/`to` arguments
each accept a bundled table name (`"human-genome"`, `"human-exome"`) or a
custom numeric vector of 96 positive finite frequencies, named by the
registry labels or matching the signature rownames. The resolver
`.ms_convert_resolve_opps()` runs TWICE -- once for `from`, once for `to`
-- so the two option arguments carry the same ten-arm validator under two
argument names, and the two abort classes split cleanly: a bad bundled
name is `msuiter_error_option`, everything else (shape, length, label
match, positivity, the signature matrix itself) is `msuiter_error_input`.
CS-18 fires 38 observation arms at it plus eight boundary-pair rows: 10
law arms, 10 acceptance specs, 10 precedence discriminators, 8 degenerate
rows (4 pairs), 10 scalars. The committed lane replays every arm live: the
law file adjudicates 233 expectations across 10 units (0 failed, 0 errors,
0 skipped, 0 warnings) and the runner rails every row against the frozen
block before any witness byte is written.

### The two option laws -- one validator, two argument names

The `from`-and-`to` split is the face's signature move, and the witness
commits it as measured. The unknown-bundled-name arm fires the SAME clause
body under each name, differing only in the leading head -- "from must be
a bundled table or a custom frequency vector" against "to must be a
bundled table or a custom frequency vector" -- and both speak the shared
[V]-discipline bullet ("panel opportunities are expected as a custom
96-vector ([V] discipline: no bundled panel table)"). The degenerate
`fromopt-vs-toopt` pair pins the two by their own clause HEADS (the
boundary contrast assertion reads `head1()` of each, split on `" | "`),
so a drift that collapsed the two heads into one reddens the lane. The
precedence roster measures the resolution ORDER: `from` resolves before
`to` (PR3), and each option law is outranked by the signature-shape law
(PR1) and the rownames law (PR2) -- the signature matrix is checked before
either opportunity argument is touched.

### The laws the face demonstrates

- **The bundled-name law.** A character scalar that is not one of the two
  bundled tables refuses as `msuiter_error_option`, naming the bundled
  roster it saw ("received: 'nope'; bundled: human-genome, human-exome").
  The panel bullet carries the [V]-discipline clause verbatim: panel
  opportunities must ride as a custom 96-vector, there is no bundled panel
  table.
- **The single-column law.** A numeric MATRIX argument with more than one
  column refuses as `msuiter_error_input` -- "from matrix must have exactly
  one frequency column" / "the opportunity is a single 96-vector, not
  per-signature" -- with the received column count ("received: 2 columns")
  and the repeat-it-yourself remedy. A one-column matrix is dropped to a
  vector and rides the acceptance path (the `onecol-vs-multicol` degen
  pair).
- **The length law.** A vector whose length is not 96 refuses -- "from must
  be a frequency vector over the 96 channels" -- carrying the received
  length ("received length: 10") and the name-or-table remedy.
- **The label law.** Names that are present but do not equal the registry
  labels refuse -- "from names must equal the SBS96 registry labels" --
  naming the first three received names and the by-label-never-by-position
  bullet. Names absent entirely are ACCEPTED (the resolver aligns by
  position when `names(opps)` is `NULL`).
- **The positivity law.** A non-finite or non-positive entry refuses --
  "from must be positive and finite" -- counting the offending entries
  against the "an opportunity of 0 makes the division undefined" bullet.
- **The signature laws.** A non-numeric or non-matrix `signatures`
  argument refuses -- "signatures must be a numeric matrix" -- naming the
  received class and the `96 x k` remedy; a matrix whose rownames are
  missing or out of canonical order refuses -- "signatures must carry the
  SBS96 registry rownames in canonical order" -- naming the first three
  rownames (or "rownames missing") and the by-label bullet.
- **Precedence.** Ten discriminators, each with its fires anchor pinned
  PRESENT and its anti anchor pinned ABSENT in the same live message --
  signature-shape before the `from` option law, rownames before the `to`
  option law, `from` before `to`, length before labels, and the
  multi-column law before the label law.
- **The acceptance specs.** The canonical `96 x 3` matrix render commits
  its full identity line (`matrix|96x3|double|TRUE|S1,S2,S3|1,1,1`) -- the
  `TRUE` committing that rownames are present and canonical, the
  `S1,S2,S3` the column roster, and `1,1,1` the discrete column-sum glyph
  (every column still sums to 1). A zero column commits its `0` glyph
  (`1,0,1`); an integer-vector plant commits the `double` storage glyph
  exactly where a silent coercion would erase it; and replaying the
  committed spec through `ms_convert()` reproduces it byte-for-byte -- the
  replay-identity spec welds two renders with `==`. The `MsSignature`
  method commits the S7 branch (`MsSignature|96x3|double|1,1,1|3x2`, the
  `3x2` being the exposure shape carried through untouched).

### The receipts

| receipt | committed bytes |
|---|---|
| `cs18_specs.tsv` | 10 accepted arms: class token `s7:matrix` (eight matrix accepts) or `s7:msuiter::MsSignature` (the S7 branch) plus the full identity rendering (shape, storage glyph, canonical-rownames bit, column roster, discrete glyph) and the `s7:character` replay identity |
| `cs18_laws.tsv` | 10 arms: class split `msuiter_error_option` (the two bundled-name arms) and `msuiter_error_input` (the eight shape/length/label/positivity/signature arms), every clause verbatim, every mode `reject` |
| `cs18_precedence.tsv` | 10 discriminators, each with its fires anchor PRESENT and its anti anchor ABSENT in the live message |
| `cs18_degenerates.tsv` | 4 boundary pairs (8 rows): the accepted zero-column glyph against the restored full column, the accepted one-column `from` matrix against the two-column one, the `from`-option law against the `to`-option law by their own heads, the shape law against the label law -- hi and lo committed side by side |
| `cs18_scalars.tsv` | 10 keys: the abort class, both renders, both storage glyphs, the round-trip-under-tolerance and same-under-tolerance verdicts, and both RNG-purity rails (the adjudication core never seeds) |

The 38-row class census (`msuiter_error_input=17`, `msuiter_error_option=8`,
`s7:matrix=11`, `s7:msuiter::MsSignature=1`, `s7:character=1`, over the four
committing rosters) is recomputed from the frozen vectors inside the law
file -- a silent class shift reddens the lane, not the reader. All five
witnesses byte-reproduce on consecutive runner invocations, the plant and
spec corpora hash identically under BOTH governed SHA-256 kernels
(`.ms_fit_sha256` and digest), and the lane never touches the RNG, the
network, the benchmark driver, the declined calibration family, or any
unexported internal (banned-word rails over the hand-written region,
marker-scoped and grepped).

### The single-source build, and the audit that became the minter

Both hosts -- law file and runner -- carry one byte-identical frozen block
and one byte-identical shared code block, each injected from a single
source between BEGIN/END markers; the splice rail demands the exact marker
counts and compares the two regions across the files byte for byte. The
minter IS the audit: every one of the 38 roster plants and the 8
text-twins is re-fired LIVE through the canonical pipeline against the
audited probe ledger (38 rows, 20 rejects / 18 accepts, DET across two
probe runs); each of the 10 precedence-path arms carries an explicit
decision-record path whose FIRES/ANTI alignment is asserted
order-invariantly; every scalar is re-fireable and re-fired; and a final
RE-AUDIT re-sources the EMITTED block into a cleared namespace and
re-compares every committed literal against the ledger -- so emitter
drift, chunking drift and quoting drift all die at mint time, not at read
time. The committed clause bytes in this page are read from the committed
witnesses, never re-typed from plan.

### What the lane-building itself caught (the honest section)

The live replay killed a would-be-innocent bug before one witness byte was
trusted. The runner's degenerate rail for the `fromopt-vs-toopt` pair had
been drafted to compare `head1(.w("from-bad-hi"))` against the literal
`"from must be a bundled table"` -- one clause short. But `head1()` splits
the message on `" | "` and returns the WHOLE first clause, which is "from
must be a bundled table or a custom frequency vector". The first runner
invocation died on the rail's own `stopif` ("degen: the from-option head
moved") -- the rail caught its own draft, exactly as intended. The fix was
applied to BOTH the runner tail and the U7 unit in the assemblers (never
hand-edited in place) and the lane regenerated: the boundary contrast now
compares the true clause heads, and the runner reached `OVERALL PASS`. The
incident is why the boundary-contrast assertions are split `" | "`-aware
rather than substring-based: a substring rail would have passed the short
literal vacuously.

### Provenance

The frozen block and the shared code block in both hosts are minted
mechanically from the audited probe ledger (audit green: 38 arms
byte-exact on live re-fire, 8 degen twins, 10/10 fires-and-anti anchors,
10 scalars re-fired); neither is ever hand-edited in place. The plants'
canonical texts hash to the committed dual-kernel checksum
(`plant_sha256=8956916dfe9065c5...`, `spec_sha256=82469f962fbe4a3b...`);
reifying the lane reproduces every witness byte for byte. Differentiation
from CS-17 (the governance-container face): CS-17 adjudicated an in-memory
container behind S7 property gates; CS-18 adjudicates a converter whose
accepted arms return a real matrix and whose two option arguments carry
one validator under two names -- the D11 posture therefore rides a DISCRETE
column-sum glyph, the first witness class in the series that had to commit
a glyph rather than a class token for its accepting arms.

### Gate forensics

The scenarios leg for this lane (the seventeenth) was render-verified
before the full local burn. The T0 seal moved 626 -> 627 with the
generator's refusal witnessed verbatim (the DEFECT line naming 627 against
the sealed 626, run against a doctored budget) before the deliberate
re-seal, per the budget law; the reified manifest carries 112 files, the
new law file on shard 4, byte-deterministic on re-mint.
